claims.claim: defineModule({ name, imports, providers, exports }) declares a module; it sees its own providers and the exports of the modules it imports
Nexus.create awaits every async useFactory, so get() stays synchronous after startup
provide(token, { useExisting: otherToken }) points one token at another so both resolve to one instance; it takes no lifetime

notApplicable.scoped: inRequestScope is one instance per resolution graph, and the docs present no per-request child container.

claims.claim: reads design:paramtypes only where no @inject token is given
new ContainerModule((options) => ...) groups bindings, and container.load(...modules) loads them; a ContainerModule has no imports or exports, so every binding is visible everywhere
container.load is synchronous and loadAsync is its async counterpart
toResolvedValue(factory, [ids]) takes a factory that receives the resolved services and may return a Promise
getAsync resolves a service whose binding builds asynchronously
Container's jitless option defaults to true; false enables JIT resolution for better performance where unsafe-eval is permitted
bind(id).toService(otherId) resolves a service identifier to the service bound under another; it takes no scope

notApplicable.async-factory: tsyringe 4.10.0 declares no async resolution: resolve() returns the instance and the README documents no async provider.

claims.claim: throws 'tsyringe requires a reflect polyfill.' at import without one
@registry([...]) on a class registers its providers when the class's module is imported
{ token, useToken } is a token provider, a redirect or an alias from one token to another

libraries.moduleNote: awilix documents no module unit. Each graph module is a register<Module>(container) function making one documented container.register({...}) call; the function is plain code the README neither shows nor forbids.

notApplicable.async-factory: awilix 13.0.5 resolves synchronously, and its README sends asynchronous init to awilix-manager (https://github.com/jeffijoe/awilix#ecosystem).

claims.claim: CLASSIC injection mode breaks under minification
container.register({...}) registers many resolvers in one call
aliasTo('name') registers a resolver that resolves another registration by name

libraries.moduleNote: needle-di documents no module unit. Each graph module is a register<Module>(container) function making one documented container.bindAll(...) call; the function is plain code the docs neither show nor forbid.

claims.claim: container.bindAll(...) binds any number of providers in one call
